description: AI pipeline that generates 7 custom prospect assets after Call 1 to increase Call 2 show rates for Quantum Scaling reps

current_state.status: V2 feature-complete and reviewed twice by Gary. Rep controls which case studies appear, which one the tab opens on, and can override the ROI quality floor deliberately. Deck generates 8/9 prospect-specific beats with a missing Proof beat hidden from prospects. All 7 Grok fixes done. Static handler hardened.

project_overview.what: Deal Forge is an internal sales tool for Quantum Scaling reps. After completing a Call 1 (Business Audit), the rep triggers the app with the Fireflies meeting ID. An AI pipeline extracts the prospect's ICP and business context, then generates 7 custom assets: a verified lead list, interactive Google Calendar invite visual, 3 webinar title options, an interactive ROI calculator pre-populated with their numbers, a prospect research profile, and brand-scraped visual identity. All assets are ready before Call 2. The in-portal Webinar Experience tab renders a one-slide branded hero + ICP-aware live chat at view time (no separate pipeline task).
project_overview.why: QS's Call 2 show rate is 37.5% — the core constraint on revenue. Prospects feel informed after Call 1 and have no strong pull to return. Deal Forge creates a concrete bridge: assets so specific to the prospect that skipping Call 2 means walking away from something already built for them. The 'sunk cost' and perceived value dramatically increase show rate and close rate.
project_overview.end_state: A polished internal rep dashboard used for every Call 2 booking. Rep selects today's calls from auto-loaded Fireflies meetings, clicks Generate, and has a full asset package ready within 20 minutes. The ROI model and reg page mock have shareable prospect-facing URLs. Eventually expands to full CRM integration and automated follow-up.
project_overview.current_summary: Phase 2 backend live on Render. 7-task pipeline deployed (webinar_mock task removed 2026-05-12 — standalone HTML asset was unused; in-portal Webinar Experience tab now renders a single brand-colors hero + ICP-aware chat client-side). Rep portal live at deal-forge-angel.onrender.com. Key systems confirmed working: (1) Fireflies transcript lookup — 6-pass search strategy (GHL name → company → email segments → domain → recent scan p1 → p2), prefers exact email match → domain match → loose keyword. (2) GHL contact lookup — enriches contactInfo with name/company/title before Fireflies search for better matching. (3) extractBriefFromTranscript — Claude Sonnet extracts full structured brief: prospect info, ICP (apollo_titles, apollo_industries, apollo_employee_ranges, apollo_geography, person_seniorities), metrics (LTV/close/show rate), angle (pain/result/methodology/proof), verbatim quotes, situation, context, webinar title seeds. (4) /api/prefetch endpoint — runs Fireflies + GHL + website scrape + Claude extraction before job creation so rep can review the brief. (5) Task handlers wired: extract, prospect_research, brand_scrape, lead_list, webinar_titles, roi_model, calendar_visual. Main blocker: lead_list EU Apollo coverage — org search returns 0 for Baltic/EU ICPs. Latest fix deployed (commit c934325): strip 'Europe' from geo (invalid Apollo value), EU country list retry with no AND-logic industry filter, geoUsed flag tells classifier to accept EU-wide companies. Unconfirmed — stopped testing to avoid rate limit loop.

resume_here: webinar_titles legacy 4-field schema removed 2026-05-14. Root cause of schema-drift regressions: loadCopyBrain rendered few-shot examples as Title+Description blob, training Claude to ignore the 12-field schema. Fix: (1) parseExampleDescription splits stored example blobs into 12 fields at prompt-build time so examples teach the new shape; (2) handleCalendarVisual composes description from the 9 narrative fields, drops `variant.description ‖ hook+bullets+for_line` fallback; (3) renderer drops `‖ v.hook` fallback; (4) spec §5 rewritten to canonical 12-field schema; (5) per-variant shape guard in generateWebinarTitles hard-fails on legacy/incomplete shape — no retry, surfaces regressions visibly. No DB migration. Test plan: trigger fresh webinar_titles on a job, confirm all 12 content fields + _score + _analysis present; re-run on 4c57375a-72c4-4fb3-be0e-5ab7d75cea54 manually to repair. Previous lead_list EU Apollo blocker still open (separate workstream).

recent_milestones.description: Three of the five items from the 2026-09-24 sales training spec. (4) THE SELECT/DESELECT BUG, which was mine: in auto mode the picker renders every box ticked while the pins array is empty, so an untick fell through to the 'not in pins' branch and PUSHED the id - making the client you just deselected the only one shown. That is the five minutes Alex lost. A first deselect in auto mode now means 'all of them except this one'. Verified: deselect removes the right tab, a second deselect removes another, re-ticking restores. (3) The live-chat panel was already restored earlier; the remaining half was the hardcoded 847 - the chat subtitle and the top bar now take the attendee number the ROI model forecasts for this prospect (300 on TrackDeep) and update whenever the rep changes an ROI input. (5) 1,400 -> 1,500 across six copy variants plus prompts/webinar_titles_system.txt so newly generated copy carries the right figure; the diff was audited line by line because a blind numeric replace could have hit a market size - and indeed two rendered '1,400' hits turned out to be '1,400,000', a client's TAM, not the claim. NOT DONE, and both are substantial: (1) the six-tab restructure (bold claim / problem + cost of INACTION combined / dream state at 3 months and a year / journey with the four risk removals / solution / three CTAs) which changes the extract contract again, and (2) real graphics beyond the current schematic motifs.

The webinar deck carries the prospect's brand colours through every beat, not just the hero. The beats were hardcoded to Quantum Scaling's green, so slide 1 was branded (TrackDeep teal #20c0c0 from the brand scrape) and slide 2 onward reverted to QS green - the jump Gary spotted. The stage gradient, the step label, the SVG motifs (drawn with currentColor, so one declaration brands them all), the close CTA and the active pill now read --prospect-primary / --prospect-primary-alpha, the same variables the hero already used, with the old values as fallbacks for a job that has no brand scrape. Verified by computed style on a real job: every one of those resolves to rgb(32,192,192). Rep-only chrome (the pickers, NEEDS PROOF, YOURS · LIVE) deliberately keeps QS green - it is our UI, not the prospect's asset. NOT changed: the ROI charts, onboarding and case-study cards still use QS green, because those surfaces are shared with V1 and recolouring them would change what reps on the current flow see.

Onboarding timeline stripped back to the four phase headers per Gary. Removed the sixteen bullets under them (kickoff/ICP/angle/framework, lead pull/copy/landing page/invites, attendance review/AB tests/call framework/first closes, monthly reviews/iteration/scaling/cross-channel) plus the now-unused .ob-phase-bullets rule. Each phase keeps its icon, timeframe, name and one-line description; the milestone band above is untouched. Verified all four phases render with zero list items and no stray lists, and that the onboarding markup stays div-balanced.

Webinar beats are visual now, and the VA line is unambiguous. VISUALS: each beat gets a schematic SVG motif in a right-hand column (diverging line for the bold claim, a gap for the problem, rising bars for the cost of waiting, a curve to target for what good looks like, a before/after pair for proof, a three-node timeline for how it goes, a shield for risks, an arrow for the close). The motifs are deliberately UNLABELLED shapes: a chart with figures on it would either repeat the copy or invent numbers, and this deck is shown to a prospect's real audience. The only numeric content is real job data - beat 2 renders the ICP as chips built from apollo_titles / apollo_keyword / apollo_geography, plus the market size when the job has one (TrackDeep has none, so it correctly renders nothing). Two problems caught by sweeping every beat at two viewport widths rather than eyeballing one: the risks beat OVERFLOWED its 952x446 box with four cards plus the aside, so beats that already carry cards now keep full width (the cards are the visual); and beat 2's chips were built by splitting the rendered line, which produced a single chip holding a whole sentence about company size - they now come from the ICP fields directly, with a 28-char cap. VA COPY: Gary confirmed the five hours is the ASSISTANT'S workload and that they operate the sending tool, so the line reads 'A trained assistant does, on our automated sending tool. Around five hours of their week - near none of yours.' That closes the open question Lloyd flagged.

The Proof beat is now rep-fillable from inside the slide. Instead of a generic placeholder the unfilled beat shows the rep a prompt - 'One client result and this slide appears' - with an Add the proof button opening a four-field modal: who they were and what changed (both required), before and after (optional). Saving writes proof_client / proof_result / proof_before / proof_after overrides, composeWebinarSlides builds the beat from them with source 'rep', and the slide becomes visible to the prospect. Clearing them puts it back to hidden. The modal states the direction explicitly - one of THEIR clients, not one of ours - because this beat is shown to the prospect's own audience and is the easiest thing in the feature to get backwards. Verified the full loop: empty shows the prompt, submitting blank refuses with a reason, filled renders the copy with a 'YOURS · LIVE' badge plus an Edit button and Before/After cards, the prospect view goes 9 -> 10 slides with ZERO rep controls leaked, and removing it returns to 9. Test content was written onto the live TrackDeep job during verification and cleared afterwards.

Webinar Experience V2 now keeps the V1 shell instead of replacing it, per Gary. The deck previously hid .webinar-wrap entirely, which threw away the hero, the slide dimensions AND the live chat. The nine beats now render into ONE generated .slide sibling inside .slide-area, so: beat 1 is the untouched V1 hero (#slide-0, keeping its brand colours, host block and stats bar), every beat is the same 952x446 box, and the 280px chat panel stays beside all ten. Added Back / Next buttons with a 'n / 10' counter, disabled at each end, alongside the existing jump-to-beat pills. PROCESS NOTE WORTH REMEMBERING: applying this as a series of blind string replacements silently deleted six functions - v2RenderInviteSwap, v2ShowInvite, v2FmtInvite, v2OpenMatches, v2CloseMatches, v2RenderRoiReal - because a range-delete spanned more than I expected. The symptom was not a crash but a ReferenceError inside applyPortalVersion() that aborted ALL V2 init, so the deck silently never rendered and __V2_JOB was never set. Recovered by reverting the file to HEAD and re-applying with an assertion that the set of defined v2* functions is unchanged, plus a called-but-undefined check. Both checks are cheap and would have caught it immediately. Also retargeted v2ShowWebinar, which still pointed at the removed #v2-deck container.

The ROI booked-call floor is now overridable by a rep pin, per Gary. The floor decides the DEFAULT, it no longer vetoes the rep: /api/case-studies?floor=0 returns sub-floor clients too, every row on a gated tab is labelled below_booked_floor regardless, and the picker fetches the unfiltered list so a weak-ratio client is at least selectable. With nothing pinned the floor still picks (3 of 5 on ROI); with a pin the rep's choice wins outright, because a poor overall ratio can still be the right example for a prospect in that client's vertical and that judgement is theirs. Sub-floor rows read '2.8% booked · below 5% bar' in the picker, and a pinned sub-floor client carries a 'YOU PINNED THIS · 2.8% BOOKED' badge on the card in EDIT MODE ONLY - so the rep is reminded mid-call without the prospect ever seeing it. The endpoint still defaults to floored, so MCP and the prospect-facing render stay safe unless something explicitly asks for the full list. Verified in a browser: auto shows 3, pinning Nicole Price (2.8%) shows her with the warning, and the prospect view renders her card with zero pickers and zero warnings.

Proper example picker on the swap surfaces. The chip strip is replaced by a panel with two SEPARATE decisions, because they were being conflated: a tick to include an example, and a radio to choose which one the tab OPENS on. Previously the prospect always landed on their own invite and the rep had no way to lead with a client's. New cs_default_invite / cs_default_webinar overrides hold 'yours' or a record id; v2DefaultIndex falls back to 'yours' when the defaulted client is no longer ticked, so un-ticking cannot leave the tab opening on nothing. Each row shows the metric that matters for that surface - invite-to-registration % on Calendar Invite, attendees on Webinar Experience, attend-to-booked % on ROI - so the rep is choosing on evidence rather than on name recognition. Ticked rows are numbered in display order. ROI gets no Opens column: it shows every chosen client side by side, so there is nothing to open on. BUG FOUND BY TESTING: the picker's own reset buttons live inside the same container as the swap tabs, and the active-state loop is index-based, so it highlighted the wrong tab - the swap row is now scoped with .v2-swap-row. Also cleaned stray pins my own test runs had written onto two real jobs (TrackDeep and Fortis), which was why one swap showed 2 of 3 clients.

First real V2 job (TrackDeep, 66f1dce7) proved the deck: 8 of 9 beats came back prospect-specific and the copy is genuinely usable - bold claim, problem, cost of waiting, what good looks like, how it goes, four named risks with structural answers, and a close. Fixes from reading it: (1) the Proof beat had no case_study in the brief, so it showed 'A client who already did this' mid-deck - it is now marked source 'missing' rather than 'fallback', HIDDEN from the prospect view and shown in edit mode badged 'NEEDS PROOF · HIDDEN FROM PROSPECT'. A prospect now sees 8 clean beats renumbered 1-8; the rep sees 9 and knows which one needs writing. Slide numbering for the slide_N_* overrides still keys on the canonical beat number, not the display position. (2) Beat 2 read 'In security services, typically Any size - from small independent security firms to large system integrators.' because company_size is free text and often a whole sentence. Short values are still spliced after 'typically'; anything sentence-shaped now stands on its own line. (3) The sending-tool explainer replaced with the real console screenshot Gary supplied, downscaled 3596px/697KB to 1800px/105KB with sharp and renamed without the space; the HTML reconstruction and its CSS were removed. (4) STATIC HANDLER HARDENED, closing the item flagged in the original MCP plan: it joined the RAW url, so any filename with a space was unreachable, and everything inside __dirname was served - .env, server.js, the specs, the prompts. Now percent-decodes (with a NUL guard), resolves and contains to __dirname, and allow-lists the only legitimate surface: images under /assets and root-level .html. Grepping every served page found exactly one local asset reference, so the allow-list is tight rather than guessed. Verified: .env, server.js, package.json, CLAUDE.md, specs/ and traversal all 404; every page, asset, API route and portal deep link still 200.

Four changes from Gary's V2 review. (1) LTV renamed to Year 1 revenue per client everywhere a human reads it - portal ROI field, source row, prospect-info label, edit hint, and the ROI asset template. Internal names (roi_ltv, metrics.ltv) kept so nothing breaks, and the extract prompt now defines the field as FIRST-YEAR revenue rather than lifetime, which is closer to what it already computed. (2) 'Hermes' removed from anything rep- or prospect-facing - it reads as one of the agents. Now 'our automated sending tool'. Internal comments and function names keep the real name. (3) The 'How it gets sent' explainer replaced with a representation of the sending console itself, segmented by the prospect's OWN ICP so they see their campaign rather than a tool tour. Deliberately no invented results: status READY, 0 sent, registration and attendance columns empty. Contact counts come from their real planned outreach. Putting plausible registration numbers in front of a prospect would be fabricating results. (4) THE EMBARRASSING-MATH FIX: 'Use on tabs' in Airtable says a client has usable artifacts, not that their numbers read well. One cleared client sits at 4 booked calls from 866 attendees (0.5%) across 19 runs, directly next to another at 9.9% - a prospect doing that arithmetic concludes the product does not work. The prototype excluded that client by hand; there is now an explicit attend-to-booked floor (ROI_MIN_BOOKED_PCT, default 5%) on the ROI tab, strongest-first. Rows are HIDDEN, never rewritten. On Webinar Experience the fix was different: that tab is proved by the recording, so the booking ratio was dropped from the card entirely and attendees kept (866 across 19 runs is a strong number on its own) - which keeps all three recordings instead of the floor cutting it to one. (5) REP CONTROL over case-study selection, per Gary overruling the auto-only design: pins stored per surface as cs_pin_* override arrays of airtable_record_id in display order. Auto-match stays the default; a pin overrides it; an 'auto' button clears back. The picker renders only when IS_EDIT_MODE - verified the prospect view renders zero pin controls.

Two defects closed that were shipped broken. (1) The deck's rep-override path was DEAD: composeWebinarSlides() reads _overrides.slide_N_headline / slide_N_sub, but PATCH /api/jobs/:id/overrides has a strict allow-list that silently drops unknown keys - so nobody could ever write the value the renderer was looking for, and a beat badged GENERIC could not be replaced. Both were described as working. Fixed by allow-listing slide_1..9_headline/_sub; verified by round-trip (write -> deck reports source 'override' -> clear -> back to fallback). (2) The MCP had ZERO knowledge of the case-study library even though /api/case-studies had been live for days - the list_case_studies tool promised when the endpoint landed was never added. Now added (tab-gated list, or the auto-matched pair for a job) with the records slimmed, since the full rows carry long narrative fields that would swamp an agent's context. Its description carries the direction warning: this library is QS's own clients proving OUR results to the prospect, while the deck's proof beat is one of the PROSPECT'S clients and must never be filled from it. MCP is now 21 tools, and set_overrides advertises the 18 slide fields.

Closed the last two V2 gaps. WEBINAR EXPERIENCE case-study swap - the fourth surface in Ryan's design, which had been missed: three clients are cleared for that tab and all three have recordings on file. Unlike the invite swap there is no copy to show, so a client only appears when a recording actually exists - the tape is what proves this tab (Alex, 2026-09-04 at 1:01:09). Shows their title, quote where present, campaign funnel, and a link out to the recording. CASE STUDIES TAB now reads the synced library under V2 (33 clients with quote, best-used-for, market size and which tabs each is cleared for) while V1 keeps its hand-maintained list, so the tab can no longer drift from what the other four surfaces show. Also moved the .v1-when-v2-hidden handling out of v2RenderDeck into applyPortalVersion - it had been hiding superseded V1 blocks as a side effect of the deck rendering, which meant it depended on which tab the rep opened first. And refreshed the dashboard V2 hint, which still described the whole redesign as in-progress after it had shipped.

Grok fix #7 closed - prefetch durability. The prefetch / extract-brief progress ids lived only in an in-process Map, so an MCP client that prefetched and then hit a Render redeploy got a permanent 404 with no recovery; a rep has a retry button, an agent does not. New sales_assets.progress_jobs table backs them. The Map stays as a write-through cache because these are polled every second or two and a row read per poll is waste; the table is the fallback when the id is not in this instance's memory, which covers both a redeploy and a second instance taking the poll. Writes are throttled to 700ms, with terminal states always flushed immediately since that is the write a poller is waiting on. THE SUBTLE PART: _extras.candidatesById is a Map, and JSON.stringify turns a Map into {} - persisting it naively would have silently dropped every transcript candidate and left extract-brief with nothing to bind to, with no error anywhere. Converted explicitly both ways. _extras is also mutated directly on the cached object in two places, bypassing setProgress, so both needed their own flush. Proved by restarting the process mid-flight: an id that returned 404 before now returns 200 with all 4 candidates and its suggested pick, and extract-brief still binds to it. Rows sweep after 6 hours. Also fixed: the V1/V2 switch only existed in step 2 of the New Job modal, which is unreachable without first running a prefetch and picking a transcript - so the person who needed it to test V2 could never find it. Now at step 1 as well, both controls sharing state. FOLLOW-UP: the first production deploy of this persisted the row but LOST the extras, while the identical local run kept them. Cause was a race, not a serialisation bug: each write sends the whole record, so two overlapping writes are last-one-lands rather than a merge, and the terminal setProgress fires microseconds before the _extras flush. Un-awaited, the earlier write (no extras yet) landed second and erased the candidate cache. Writes for one id are now chained. Worth remembering that the API reported success in both cases - only reading the row showed the difference.

Remaining three V2 surfaces built. ROI 'Real client results': campaign TOTALS across every run a client did, ordered by how close their market is to the prospect's, closest badged. No dollar figure is shown anywhere - no client has LTV or close rate on file, so a revenue number would be invented; funnel and booked calls only. Lead List: a '> Clients with a market like yours' link under the TAM opens a modal of matched clients (market axis + offering axis) - a pop-up, tab itself unchanged, per Lloyd's 2026-09-05 call. Calendar Invite 'The invite': a 'Show invite: Yours | <client>' switcher that swaps in a real client's VERBATIM copy, never generated and never blended with QS's offer (the failure Alex named at 42:28). event_description is rendered from plain text with ALL-CAPS lines as headings and bullet glyphs as list items, matching how it is stored. THE BUG WORTH REMEMBERING: a rep-typed TAM reaches the code as a STRING ('1.1M'), because the portal stores isNaN(Number(v)) ? v : Number(v). Number() on that is NaN, which silently disabled the closest-market ordering on ROI AND the entire TAM match axis on Lead List, and printed 'your market of NaN' in the modal. Fixed on both sides with parseHumanNumber/_v2ParseNum. Nothing threw; it just quietly did nothing - only visible by rendering it.

Nine-beat webinar deck built. Extract prompt extended with a 'webinar' section carrying one object per beat (bold_claim, problem, cost_of_waiting, good_looks_like, case_study, how_it_goes, risks, close), written from the seat of the PROSPECT'S ICP - the person who watches the webinar - not from QS's seat. Slide 6 is explicitly the prospect's OWN client and must never be filled from the QS Airtable library; the direction is opposite to Lead List / Calendar Invite. composeWebinarSlides() assembles all nine server-side and returns them on GET /api/jobs/:id, so portal and MCP see the same deck. Beat 2 is composed from the ICP rather than written by the model. Every beat the extractor could not support falls back to generic reference copy tagged source:'fallback' and badged GENERIC in the UI - a rep reading invented specifics aloud to a prospect is worse than a rep seeing an honest placeholder. Rep overrides (slide_N_headline / slide_N_sub) win over both. Three bugs caught in testing, none of which a unit test would have found: the close slide spliced the entire offer_description paragraph into a sentence (offering_name only now, capped at 40 chars); beat 2 produced 'You are owner in professional services' because icp.role is documented as a noun phrase but in practice holds a comma list of titles (now rendered as a seat list, no article or pluralisation to get wrong); and the deck initially double-showed the message because the V1 hero stayed visible (now hidden under V2). VA copy corrected per Gergo: QS either places a trained assistant OR trains someone already on the client's team - the card previously claimed only the former. Open question still unanswered: whether 'around five hours a week' is the assistant's workload or the client's involvement.

Case-study library synced and first V2 surfaces shipped. SYNC: first real Airtable pull succeeded in 88s - 33 clients, 21 transcripts, 8 clips, 56 headshots/logos re-hosted into Supabase Storage. Data is far richer than the prototype fixtures implied: 32 with TAM, 19 with a webinar title, 18 with invite copy, 15 with campaign stats, 25 with a key quote. Real tab gating from 'Use on tabs': Lead List / TAM 21, ROI Model 5, Calendar Invite 3, Webinar Experience 3. Also widened the token lookup to four env spellings after AIRTABLE_API_KEY silently never reached the service, and added an airtable_env_seen diagnostic (names + lengths only, never values) that separated 'typo' from 'never arrived' in one call. V2 UI: Calendar Invite now has an outreach sub-tab group - 'The invite' (existing calendar, unchanged), 'How it gets sent' (Hermes calendar-automation explainer) and 'Who runs it' (Alex's VA script verbatim from the 2026-09-04 training at 59:53, with the three proof clients' real headshots from our synced library rather than expiring Airtable links). All .v2-only nodes stay display:none until applyPortalVersion() sees portal_version==='v2' - verified in a browser that a V1 job renders zero V2 nodes. Two polish fixes from browser testing: the portal's escHtml() lives in a different script block so V2 carries its own escaper, and library company names hold internal research annotations that had to be stripped for a prospect-facing tab. NOT yet built: invite copy swap, Lead List match modal, ROI real client results, the 9-slide deck, and the extract extension it needs.

Grok MCP smoke-test fixes + case-study library groundwork + V1/V2 flow switch. FIXES (from the Andy Viikmaa / TrackDeep smoke job): (1) icp.geography no longer holds prose — extract wrote 'Global, with near-term focus on civilian markets; US market entry discussed' into the Company Location filter while apollo_geography stayed null, so the rep saw a location and Apollo got none; geography is now DERIVED from apollo_geography, prose is parked on geography_note, the extract prompt forbids it, and PATCH /icp mirrors apollo_geography→geography the way it already mirrored apollo_keyword→industry. (2) prefetch Call-1 ranking: recency was the tiebreak so a 51-min '3rd Meeting' beat the 39-min 'Business Evaluation Call'; added call1Score (title match, later-meeting penalty, 35-90min band, prospect-on-call check) folded into the sort as rankOf*10+score so tiers stay dominant — BE now scores 105 vs 0. (3) MCP tool copy flipped: prefetch_prospect is the recommended first step, bare-email create_job is the shortcut. (4) rerun_tam 500 fixed — apollo_keyword can be an array and (x||y||'').trim() blew up; added icpIndustryTerms/Label/Seed, single-element arrays collapse byte-identically to the old string path. (5) TAM auto-escalation: Apollo-exact below TAM_ESCALATION_FLOOR (30k, env-tunable) now spawns the grounded LLM TAM and stamps _tam_auto_escalated, since a narrow count reads as disqualifying (Ryan showed 55k where Apollo-narrow was 23k); never overrides a manual tam_total. (6) parseLtv now handles prose — '€11,500 first year (€10,000 sensor + €1,500 subscription)' → 11500, ranges → midpoint, percentages still rejected; and handleRoiModel now honours _overrides.roi_ltv, which it never did, so setting the override could not previously unblock a needs_input rerun. NOT done: (7) prefetch durability (Grok marked it nice-to-have). 27 unit assertions across the helpers, all passing against Grok's verbatim inputs. LIBRARY: migration 20260911_case_study_library creates case_study_clients / _transcripts / _clips / _sync_state mirroring the 33-record 'Customer Testimonials' Airtable base (field list read off the live base). airtable-sync.js pulls all three tables, upserts on airtable_record_id, and RE-HOSTS headshots and logos into Supabase Storage because Airtable attachment URLs expire within hours — storing them would break every logo the same day. Re-download is skipped when the source filename is unchanged. MCP connectors became multi-tenant and moved under Settings → Integrations (alongside Zoom), replacing the single-row mcp_config shipped hours earlier. New sales_assets.mcp_connectors: one row per agent with name, token_hash, token_prefix, enabled, allow_delete, last_used_at, rotated_at, plus a partial unique index on token_hash so two connectors can never share a token and auth resolves to exactly one row. Migration 20260910_mcp_connectors carries over any live token from the old singleton before dropping it, so an already-connected bot would not break (nothing to carry in practice — no token had been generated). Rationale: the singleton could only ever describe one bot, and Deal Forge has no way to know what is on the far end of a token, so a user-typed name is the only thing that identifies a connection — hence name + last_used_at as the two things the UI leans on. Auth now hashes the presented bearer and compares against every ENABLED connector with timingSafeEqual and no early break (uniform work across the small list); the matched row becomes the request's cfg, so allow_delete is per connector and the audit line carries connector=<name>. last_used_at is throttled per connector id. Routes replaced: GET/POST /api/admin/mcp-connectors, PATCH + DELETE /:id, POST /:id/rotate, GET /test — none ever return a token except create and rotate, which return it exactly once. DEALFORGE_MCP_TOKEN now behaves as an extra always-on connector rather than an override, and the UI surfaces it when set. Verified: two connectors authenticate independently; granting delete to one gives it CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED while the other still gets DELETE_DISABLED (job never deleted); disabling one leaves the other working; rotating one retires only its own token; the list response never contains a live token; and the UI was driven in headless Chromium end to end (add, one-time reveal, test, remove) with zero console errors. Test connector rows were deleted afterwards — mcp_connectors left empty.

Settings → Connectors: MCP connector managed from the UI instead of Render env vars. New singleton sales_assets.mcp_config (migration 20260910, applied + verified) storing ONLY sha256(token) plus a 14-char prefix, enabled, allow_delete, label, last_used_at, rotated_at. Storing the token in plaintext was rejected: every /api/* route is unauthenticated, so a plaintext column would be world-readable via GET /api/admin/mcp-config and would make the bearer check on /mcp pointless — so the token is returned exactly once, by the rotate call, the same trade GitHub PATs make. Four routes added next to zoom-config/sop-config: GET /api/admin/mcp-config (status + tool list, never the token), PUT (enabled/allow_delete/label), POST /rotate (mint, invalidates the previous token immediately, auto-enables), POST /revoke, and GET /test (probes /mcp anonymously — a 401 proves live-and-gated, which is all we can assert since we hold only the hash). mcp-server.js now resolves its config through a loader injected by server.js via configure({loadConfig, touchLastUsed}), so it still imports nothing from server.js; 30s cache invalidated on every write so a toggle takes effect immediately; allow_delete is threaded per-request through dispatch → callTool → tool.run rather than read from a module const. DEALFORGE_MCP_TOKEN still works and OVERRIDES the UI as a break-glass path, and the settings screen says so when it is in effect. Fail-closed preserved: no token or connector off ⇒ 503 for everyone, with a message pointing at the settings screen. Verified in a real browser via Playwright (headless Chromium, scratchpad-only — not added to project deps): tab switch, config load, Generate token, one-time reveal box, Copy full Grok config, Test connection, toggles, and revoke, with zero JS console errors; plus API-level proof that allow_delete=false ⇒ DELETE_DISABLED, allow_delete=true ⇒ stops at CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED (job NOT deleted), revoke invalidates instantly, and the token string never appears in any GET response. Test tokens minted against the shared production database during verification were revoked afterwards; mcp_config left clean (token cleared, disabled).

Remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP, stateless) mounted at /mcp inside server.js — first authenticated route in the app. 20 tools wrapping the existing HTTP API over loopback (127.0.0.1) rather than calling internals, so MCP behaviour cannot drift from what the dashboard gets: route logic lives inline in the if-chain and is not callable as functions. HAND-ROLLED JSON-RPC, zero new dependencies. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk was installed, evaluated and removed: 87 transitive packages (express 5, hono, jose, ajv, cors, express-rate-limit, zod) into a 3-dependency app, and its Node transport wraps @hono/node-server which reads req.rawHeaders not req.headers — so the standard `req.headers.accept = ...` interop fix is a silent no-op and the transport hard-406s any client not sending both application/json and text/event-stream (webStandardStreamableHttp.js:471, not disableable). We content-negotiate instead: verified working with Accept of application/json, text/event-stream, both, */* and absent. AUTH: Authorization: Bearer against DEALFORGE_MCP_TOKEN, sha256+timingSafeEqual, fail-closed 503 when unset or <32 chars (never degrades to open). GUARDRAILS are server-side because xAI does not support MCP require_approval: 9 tools need confirm:true (rerun_apollo, rerun_tam, reveal_lead=1 Apollo credit, regenerate_webinar_titles, rescan_brand_colors, start_or_continue_pipeline, prefetch_prospect, extract_brief, delete_job); delete_job additionally needs DEALFORGE_MCP_ALLOW_DELETE=1, off by default. callApi normalises the four envelope shapes the app returns — bare arrays, {ok:true,...}, raw rows, and HTTP 200-carrying-an-error (/api/prefetch/:id, /api/extract-brief/:id, /api/zoom/test) — so an agent can never read a 200 as success. get_job is compact by default with heavy sections opt-in via include[], results capped at 90KB with an explicit truncation marker. Two parity bugs found and fixed during testing: (1) GET /api/jobs/:id does not return the assigned rep (only the list endpoint does), so get_job now merges both; (2) tam_total/roi_* were typed as number, but the portal stores whatever isNaN(Number(v))?v:Number(v) yields — a rep can type '1.1M' — so the schema accepts number|string and mirrors that coercion (mockup-portal.html:3145). Inserted ABOVE the blanket OPTIONS handler because that handler answers 204 for every path with an Allow-Headers list of Content-Type only, which would reject an MCP preflight carrying Authorization. Verified: 11/11 protocol sweep (auth, 405, 204, tools/list, ping, notifications 202, confirm gate, path-traversal rejection, -32602/-32601, JSON-RPC batch), write path proven idempotently against a live job (set_overrides, assign_rep, update_brief writing back identical values), and all existing routes + portal regression-checked unchanged. NOT yet deployed — needs DEALFORGE_MCP_TOKEN set in the Render dashboard before the deploy lands.

Even title distribution in the Apollo lead list. Reported on kjartan@noona.app: rep entered ~10 titles, the 25-lead sample came back ~90% 'Tattoo Artist'. Root cause was title-blindness at BOTH retrieval and selection: (a) fetchLeadsFromApollo sends every title as one person_titles OR-array, and Apollo ranks the union by its own relevance, which is dominated by whichever title has the biggest population; (b) the email-coverage pagination loop stops the moment 25 unique companies exist, so in a dense market page 1 IS the pool; (c) finalizeLeadList then deduped by company and sliced 25 with no title awareness. Re-ordering alone could not fix it — the pool itself was single-title. FIX, two halves. RETRIEVAL: new STEP 5 'per-title balancing fan-out' in guaranteedLeadSearch — after the payload settles, fire one page-1 search per title with person_titles narrowed to that single title, tagging each result with _matched_title. Apollo search costs 0 credits so this is latency-only; bounded by MAX_FANOUT_TITLES=15, FANOUT_CONCURRENCY=5 (matches peopleMatchAllLeads), FANOUT_BUDGET_MS=12000 (deliberately below apolloPeopleSearch's 15s AbortSignal so a stalled Apollo costs exactly one wave). Best-effort: apolloPeopleSearch swallows its own errors, so a dead slice contributes nothing and the worst case is the previous behaviour. Fan-out results are kept in a separate array so the MAX_PAGES pool cap can never trim them. SELECTION: new balanceLeadsByTitle() does person-dedupe + title round-robin + company-dedupe in one pass, replacing the old company-only dedupe at the top of finalizeLeadList. Key details, each fixing a way the balance would otherwise leak: person dedupe UNIONS the fan-out's _matched_title tags onto the surviving copy (first-wins keeps the untagged combined-pool copy, and with include_similar_titles set the tag is the only ground truth for leads like 'Body Modification Specialist' from a Piercer slice); buckets are a UNION not a partition, since real titles are compound ('Business Owner/ Tattoo Artist') and each lead is still consumed exactly once; has_email leads float to the front of each bucket (stable sort) so the balance survives the downstream has_email partition and reveal loop; buckets rotate scarcest-first so an abundant title cannot drain a scarce overlapping subset; and the company claim is folded INTO the rotation so a company collision makes that bucket advance to its next candidate instead of forfeiting the slot. Title matching normalizes via NFD + combining-mark strip before a Unicode-class filter (EU chips fan out to 27 countries, so 'Geschaeftsfuehrer' must fold), and uses whole-word-sequence containment, which subsumes splitTitleParts. DIAGNOSTICS: title_mix {counts, pool_counts, unmatched} on the lead_list output and in apollo_diagnostics (counts seeded with every searched title so a dead chip reads as 0, and pool_counts separates 'no such people here' from 'companies ran out'); server log line '[lead_list] Title mix (final 25)'; rep-only mix row above the lead table in mockup-portal.html derived from the _title_bucket stamped on each lead. Also capped harvestLeadTitlesToCorpus input at 300 leads — it does an unbounded Promise.all of tag lookups per unique title part, and the ~3x bigger pool would have turned into a few hundred concurrent GETs at Apollo's tags endpoint. Both callers (handleLeadList and POST /api/jobs/:id/rerun-apollo) covered via the shared helpers; <2 titles degenerates byte-for-byte to the old behaviour. Verified with 31 assertions against the helpers extracted verbatim from server.js (90%-dominant pool -> even 3-4 per live title; email-poor scarce titles still reach the emailed tier at full depth; company collisions do not cost slots; tag survives dedupe; accent folding; degenerate inputs unchanged). NOT yet run against live Apollo — needs a rerun on the kjartan@noona.app job to confirm end-to-end.

TAM PLANNER FIX (after first local test showed a weak LLM number): root causes were (a) the LLM kept the narrow industry keyword on every slice — the single biggest under-counter (REACHUM: 1,378 with 'pharmaceuticals' vs 31,131 without) — and (b) it emitted human department phrases ('learning and development') that Apollo silently zeroes. Fixes: rewrote TAM_PLANNER_SYSTEM to force at least one no-industry-keyword broad slice + wide title unions; added VALID_DEPARTMENTS + normalizeDepartments() (maps L&D/training/talent→human_resources etc.); added an unbounded-slice guard (rejects seniority-only slices that match millions). decision_log.decision: MCP tools call the app over loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1) instead of invoking internal functions, and the JSON-RPC layer is hand-rolled rather than using @modelcontextprotocol/sdk.
decision_log.reasoning: Loopback: the 62 route bodies live inline inside the if-chain in server.js, entangled with req/res (parseBody, query parsing off req.url, multiple res.end exit points, and at least one route that writes 202 then keeps running). Extracting them would be a multi-day refactor of the exact paths reps use daily, to save ~0.2ms against handlers that already round-trip to Supabase/Apollo/Fireflies/Anthropic. Loopback also guarantees MCP behaviour can never drift from the UI's, because it is literally the same code path. Hand-rolled: a client needs only initialize, notifications/*, ping, tools/list, tools/call. The SDK costs 87 transitive packages in a deliberately 3-dependency app and makes Accept-header correctness depend on an undocumented internal of a transitive dep (@hono/node-server reading rawHeaders). Owning ~250 lines removes the interop risk rather than working around it. Escape hatch: the module's only export is handle(req,res,urlPath), so swapping in the SDK later touches nothing in server.js — do that if server-initiated messages (sampling, elicitation) or real OAuth are ever needed.

decision_log.decision: New sales reps are added by picking their GoHighLevel user in Settings, not auto-created from GHL and not keyed on email.
decision_log.reasoning: ghl_user_id is the join key the whole pipeline already uses — GHL's opportunity assignedTo returns a user ID, and getRepByGhlUserId() joins on it. Keying on email would need a reverse email→user lookup on every job and would break whenever a rep's GHL email differs from their calendar/Fireflies email. Picking the GHL user captures the ID and the email in one action, and the email feeds getRepEmails() → transcript [REP]/[PROSPECT] labeling. Auto-creating a rep per unknown owner was rejected because the location has 78 users and only 5 are reps.
